messages:
Aisha Bello: hey folks — before we enable kernel selector v2 anywhere beyond internal, SRE needs explicit rollout guardrails + rollback criteria written down (and agreed). the current draft is a bit hand-wavy.

Aisha Bello: specifically:
- what SLO monitors are *required* during canary?
- what thresholds trigger rollback vs “watch + investigate”?
- who has authority to hit the kill switch, and what’s the expected time-to-rollback?

Aisha Bello: doc draft here (WIP): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGSRE/selector-v2-rollout-slo-guardrails

Connor O'Brien: +1. release train wise, I need numbers, not vibes :)

Allison Grant: agree. also want the “decision log” for rollbacks to be consistent. we’ve had too many “it felt spiky” rollbacks with no crisp criteria.

Grace Kim: makes sense. we can propose baseline deltas relative to selector v1 on same cohort.

Grace Kim: what we were thinking (for hosted canary):
- p95 end-to-end latency regression > +8% sustained 10 min => rollback
- p95 TTFT regression > +10% sustained 10 min => rollback
- 5xx rate +0.2% absolute over baseline sustained 5 min => rollback
- any NaN/correctness alert > 0 (after dedupe) => immediate rollback

Aisha Bello: thank you. couple questions:
1) “baseline” definition (previous 24h? previous deploy? v1 side-by-side?)
2) separate criteria for long-context buckets? (we’ve been burned by long prompts on A10)

Omar El-Sayed: baseline: we can do side-by-side on the same canary slice by keeping v1 enabled as fallback and sampling v2 vs v1 decisions in telemetry.

Omar El-Sayed: we’re instrumenting selector_version + seq_bucket (prefill/decode + context bucket), so we can scope monitors to long-context buckets.

Thomas Baird: jumping in — please don’t make the dashboards filter on raw model_id / full prompt_len. cardinality will explode.

Thomas Baird: suggested labels:
- selector_version: v1|v2
- model_family: llama|mistral|qwen|unknown
- gpu_sku: l4|a10|a100|h100|unknown
- seq_bucket: prefill_s|prefill_m|prefill_l|decode_s|decode_m|decode_l
- kernel_id: bucketed/hashed or top-N only (otherwise we’ll regret it)

Allison Grant: +1. doc should explicitly list “allowed labels” so teams don’t accidentally add model_name and page us later.

Hiro Tanaka: on rollback criteria, we should also include “crash/OOM” signals:
- runtime worker crashlooping above X/min
- CUDA OOM rate above baseline
- sudden throughput drop (tok/s) even if latency looks ok (batching can mask)

Sahana Iyer: for perf canary we’re already using budgets similar to what Grace listed, but CI is synthetic. for prod canary we should define *separate* budgets by GPU SKU.

Sahana Iyer: e.g. A10 is noisier, but we also have known sensitivity on long-context decode. might set A10 long-context p95 decode budget tighter (+5%) and rollback faster.

Connor O'Brien: +1 on SKU-specific. if we ship a single global number, we’ll argue for hours during rollout.

Aisha Bello: ok, proposal:
- primary rollback triggers should be scoped by (gpu_sku, seq_bucket) with clear thresholds.
- if any single slice violates budget, we rollback (no averaging across the fleet).

i’m going to add that to the doc unless someone objects.

Grace Kim: that’s fair. we can also include “investigate” thresholds that page runtime but don’t auto-rollback.

Grace Kim: investigate-only:
- p95 regression +4% for 10 min
- increased fallback_rate to v1 (could indicate missing registry entry)

Omar El-Sayed: we’ll add fallback_rate and “safe kernel set hit” metrics (we call it safe_set_used=true).

Allison Grant: add “unknown model family” guardrail too. if unknown_family rate spikes, that means taxonomy/mapping is broken and perf data is suspect.

Benji Okafor: on authority + procedure:
- kill switch is config flag `runtime.kernel_selector.v2.enabled=false` (global) + per-region override
- rollback path: config push + SIGHUP to runtime (no restart) — target < 5 min to take effect
- Connor (Release) + oncall SRE can flip; runtime oncall should be in the loop

Aisha Bello: can we commit that SRE oncall can flip without waiting for runtime approval if rollback criteria are met?

Benji Okafor: yes. if criteria are met, SRE oncall can flip and we’ll follow up async.

Connor O'Brien: please write that explicitly. release process wants it black-and-white.

runtime-deploy-bot: Config change detected in staging: `runtime.kernel_selector.v2.enabled=true` (team=runtime) (reaction: :eyes:)

Aisha Bello: ^ pls keep staging fine, but prod canary needs the doc merged first :)

Hiro Tanaka: +1 — we’ll add a checklist item: “SRE guardrails doc reviewed + dashboards linked” before enabling in prod.

Thomas Baird: last ask: when you add dashboards, include the “top kernels” panel but limit to top 20 by volume. otherwise the query is going to be spicy.

Allison Grant: action items:
- Grace/Omar: update confluence draft with concrete thresholds + SKU/seq bucket scope + unknown_family trigger
- Benji/Connor: document authority + expected rollback time
- Aisha: add required monitors list + links (latency, TTFT, 5xx, NaN, OOM/crashloop, fallback_rate)

Aisha Bello: works. i’ll review once updated. goal is to have this ready before the 5% us-east step.

Connor O'Brien: thanks all — ping me when the doc is in “ready for signoff” state.

Grace Kim: will do, aiming EOD.

Omar El-Sayed: same. we’ll drop the exact metric names in the doc so the dashboards match.

Aisha Bello: perfect. (reaction: :thumbsup:)
